title: Sprint Cardinal: deployment choices decision log
content:
Context: Sprint Cardinal is a 6-week proof-of-concept with a mid-market fintech (codename: Cardinal). They need conversational workflows and document understanding with strict PII controls in EU. The goal of this doc is a short, chronological decision log and a single recommended architecture plus explicit acceptance criteria and fallbacks.

High-level customer asks (from kickoff):
- 5k monthly active users, bursty peaks to ~300 concurrent inference sessions
- 99th‑percentile latency target: <400ms for short chat turns (~64 tokens)
- Data residency: EU only; some documents may be regulated (financial statements)
- Auditability: request/response logging with customer-controlled retention and KMS integration
- Budget target: keep hosted spend ~<$20k/month during POC, with agreement to evaluate Dedicated if traffic stabilizes

Audience: SEs, infra/product SMEs, and customer technical leads.

1) Chronology / decisions (short log)
- 2024-11-09 (kickoff): baseline options scoped: Hosted (multitenant), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in eu-west), Private (VPC-hosted control-plane with customer-managed network). Initial leaning: hosted for speed to value, but key questions on audit/KMS.
- 2024-11-18 (security deep-dive): customer requires KMS with CMKs per-tenant and audit timestamps stored for 7 years. Hosted default model: Redwood-managed KMS; Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS (notes: product work required for per-customer key scopes). Decision: add Dedicated as candidate; Hosted requires exception/engineering to meet KMS requirement.
- 2024-11-24 (latency sizing session): estimated per-request compute using mPT-7B-v2 derivative: p50 70ms, p95 260ms on V100-equivalent with batching disabled. Prediction: hosted zones in eu-west likely meet latency; Dedicated can reduce p95 by ~30% through reserved instances and tuned kernel selection.
- 2024-12-03 (cost workshop w/ finance): back-of-envelope POC cost: Hosted at projected 5k MAU ~ $13k/mo (tokens + infra + support), Dedicated (small reserved pool) ~ $9k/mo base but with commit + ops uplift (one-time onboarding $18k). Customer prefers Hosted to avoid upfront. Decision: proceed with Hosted POC with feature gating on KMS/audit.
- 2024-12-12 (compliance signoff required): legal flagged that logs must be under customer control for regulated documents. Hosted will only be permitted if logs can be exported to customer S3 with encryption in transit and at rest. Need to prototype.
- 2025-01-14 (prototype results): log-export prototype works; latency impact ~+20ms. Security team accepted export pipeline with per-tenant prefixes and lifecycle rules. Decision: go ahead with Hosted POC; contingency plan to move to Dedicated if access/KMS constraints arise.

2) Recommendation (single architecture)
- Primary: Hosted API in eu-west region with the following controls:
  - Per-tenant log export to customer S3 bucket using customer-managed KMS (CMK). Logs include request id, model id, input/output hashes (not full PII by default), and pointers to encrypted payloads.
  - Model pinning: pin to a quantized 7B variant with verified perf profile for latency cost balance.
  - Routing policy: prefer lowest-latency host pool within eu-west; failover to dedicated pool (if provisioned) only on capacity events.
  - Rate limiting and quota: hard quota per-minute with burst protection to protect p95 SLA.
  - Observability: enable per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdown; send aggregated traces to customer SIEM via webhook.

- Contingency: Dedicated (reserved pool) in eu-west with private network peering if Hosted cannot meet the KMS/legal constraints discovered during pilot. Dedicated runbook ensures a one-week migration window (see Runbook excerpt).

3) Acceptance criteria for POC (customer + Redwood)
- Functional: conversational flows complete without systemic failures for >99% of requests over a 48-hour soak with representative traffic.
- Latency: p95 < 450ms (measured from synthetic and sampled production) for short turns; degradation threshold 600ms triggers canary rollback.
- Security: logs exported to customer S3 using CMK; demo of audit retrieval shown to customer's compliance team.
- Cost: monthly infra+model spend <= $20k for POC period (target), with notification if trending >$15k/week.
- Ops: on-call playbook executed once during POC window; incident response time SLA for Sev2 <= 60 min.

4) Risks and mitigations (quick)
- Risk: Hosted KMS semantics differ from customer expectations (e.g., deletion/rotation semantics). Mitigation: show prototype, document differences, offer Dedicated with direct cloud KMS integration.
- Risk: Unexpected token growth driving cost. Mitigation: implement token caps, logging of long prompts, and weekly cost telemetry with auto-alerting.
- Risk: Data sovereignty edge-case where documents must never leave customer VPC. Mitigation: fallback to Private deployment but with longer lead time (~6–8 weeks) and higher cost.

5) Rough capacity/cost notes (engineering back-of-envelope)
- Workload assumptions: average session = 120 tokens in + 80 tokens out; 300 concurrent sessions peak; 6k tokens/sec processing at peak if naive.
- Hosted perf profile: one eu-west serving pod (A100-like) can service ~40 concurrent short-turn low-batch sessions with p95 ~300ms. For 300 concurrent target: recommend autoscaling target pool = 8–10 pods.
- Cost snapshot for POC (approx):
  - Hosted: model compute + infra ~ $11k/mo, bandwidth & logs ~$1.5k/mo, support $1.5k/mo => ~ $14k/mo (matches finance calc)
  - Dedicated: reserved node hourly commit ~= $7k/mo equivalent + ops/runbook/monitoring $2k/mo + onboarding one-time $18k

6) Operational notes & runbook excerpt (practical bits SEs need to know)
- Quick rollback pattern: route traffic from hosted pool -> canary variant (reduced capacity) -> previous pinned model. Use rollout window 15m with monitor for error-rate and latency.
- Failover mapping: inbound routing policy decides based on (a) latency SLO, (b) capacity headroom, (c) customer-tier flag. If capacity event -> shift small % (5–10%) to backup pool and observe for 10 minutes before full shift.
- On-call checklist (abbreviated): collect trace ids, customer S3 prefix, confirm CMK key-id, snapshot autoscaler metrics, create incident in JIRA (JIRA-OPS-...), notify customer Slack channel.

7) Open questions / TO‑DOs
- Engineering: need to confirm per-tenant CMK lifecycle operations (rotate/revoke) and any Redwood-managed control-plane limitations. Owner: Marco Ruiz. ETA: 2025-02-20.
- Product: finalize contract language for log-export SLA and retention limits. Owner: Priya Kapoor. ETA: 2025-02-05.
- SE: prepare short demo script showing how to retrieve logs from S3 and correlate with request ids. Owner: Anjali Rao. ETA: 2025-01-28 (in progress).

8) If we must recommend the Dedicated path (what changes):
- Customer-managed KMS directly attached to reserved nodes via cloud KMS IAM binding.
- Private peering for direct ingestion of documents (SFTP or API) into a dedicated secure path — reduces egress overhead and legal concerns.
- Estimated migration effort: 1 week for infra + 2 weeks for config & security signoff. One-time onboarding cost noted above.

Quick notes to self: this doc should be presented at customer steering call. Keep messaging simple: "Hosted POC for speed, Dedicated if compliance blocks hosted." Bring cost numbers and clear migration path.

References and attachments (local): prototype-notes-2025-01-14.log, latency-sample-eu-west-2024-11.csv, cost-breakdown-sheet-2024-12.xlsx

End of decision log.

-- Anjali (SE)
